summary:
AETHRA is an offline-first interactive Mars survival guide and map. It turns scattered NASA data into one guided experience where anyone can explore Mars, plan a surface walk and compare landing scenarios.

Users rotate a 3D Mars globe built from NASA Viking imagery and MOLA elevation, browse an atlas of 22 landing sites and regions, and plan a return walk using 29 archived Perseverance rover positions from Jezero Crater, with science stops, a time reserve and a return stress test. A landing planner compares seven regions using a transparent descent and fuel model. NOVA, a bilingual English and Arabic companion, answers from stored NASA knowledge and the latest NASA news, and can optionally run a local AI model without any cloud service.

Everything runs from one self-contained file, because Mars has no network and no GPS. Every claim links to NASA, and the app clearly separates NASA observations from our own assumptions. AETHRA makes Mars exploration understandable, honest and accessible.
details:
AETHRA is an offline-first interactive Mars survival guide and map, built for the challenge "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map".

WHAT IT DOES

Mars has no GPS, no road network and no live weather service. AETHRA brings the scattered NASA knowledge an explorer would need into one guided experience:

- A 3D Mars globe using NASA Viking imagery and MGS/MOLA elevation.

- A Marswalk planner built on 29 archived Perseverance rover positions (Sols 13-175) in Jezero Crater. Users add science stops, set speed, duration and a time reserve, and run a return stress test (slower return plus delay).

- A map workspace to draft waypoint walks with great-circle distances and time budgets.

- A Mars Landing Planner that compares seven regions with a transparent descent and fuel model (ballistic coefficient, atmospheric density, rocket equation).

- An atlas of 22 landing sites and orbital regions, each linked to NASA.

- NOVA, a bilingual English/Arabic companion that answers from stored NASA knowledge and, when run locally, from NASA news refreshed every 60 seconds, with an optional local language model.

- PDF reports that embed the plan so it can be reopened and edited.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

AETHRA makes Mars exploration understandable for students, educators and space enthusiasts. It shows how time, fuel, terrain and evidence shape a decision, in Arabic and English, and it works without internet.

HONESTY BY DESIGN

Every claim links to NASA. NASA observations, our model assumptions and user notes are kept separate. The app states clearly that there is no live weather, radiation or suit telemetry, that scores are not probabilities of survival, and that routes are not certified.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, Canvas and SVG, pdf-lib, a service worker, a Python 3 standard-library local server, and Ollama (optional local language model).

CREATIVITY

Planning, landing and evidence are combined in one self-contained file of about 11 MB, with disclosed equations and clear limits instead of black-box scores.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Offline operation, transparency of assumptions, bilingual and right-to-left design, dark and light themes, and a secure local server (loopback only, NASA-only fetching).
